topics.title: Enterprise Risk Management Foundations
topics.objective: The candidate will understand the foundations of ERM and be able to apply them to organizations.

outcomes.text: Describe the concept of ERM, the drivers behind it and the resulting value to organizations
Recommend an appropriate enterprise risk management framework for an organization
Analyze the ERM roles and responsibilities of the people within an organization and how the different groups can collaborate effectively
Demonstrate an understanding of governance issues, such as agency, compliance and legal risks and the need for audit and market conduct compliance activities
Evaluate the elements and structure of a successful risk management function
Examine the impact of the external environment on an organization’s ability to achieve its objectives

topics.title: Risk Analysis and Evaluation
topics.objective: The candidate will understand the types of risks faced by an entity and be able to identify and assess these risks.

outcomes.text: Identify specific risks faced by an organization
Detect emerging risks
Determine an appropriate monitoring mechanism for emerging risks
Determine the implication of risks on the balance sheet and income statement
Describe the properties and limitations of common risk measures (e.g., VaR and TVaR)
Demonstrate risk aggregation techniques that illustrate the concept of risk diversification
Demonstrate the use of scenario analysis and stress testing in the measurement of risks
Demonstrate the use of techniques to assess risk accumulations and compounding risks
Demonstrate an understanding of model risk
Propose an appropriate modelling technique that meets organizational needs to analyze risks
Analyze risks that are not easily quantifiable, such as operational, environmental and contagion-related risks

topics.title: Embedding ERM into Decision-Making
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how an organization can articulate its approach to risk and how to assess risk and return trade-offs. The candidate will understand the approaches for managing risk. The candidate will understand different concepts of risk capital, risk measures in capital assessment and techniques to allocate risk capital once aggregated.

outcomes.text: Describe how an organization can articulate its approach to risk using risk appetite and risk limits
Assess the risk and return trade-offs for decisions (e.g. those targeting changes in the organization’s risk profiles)
Demonstrate application of the following responses to risk, including consideration of their costs and benefits: avoidance, acceptance, reduction without transfer, and transfer to a third party
Demonstrate the use of controls in an organizational process
Demonstrate how derivatives or similar methods may be used to manage or reduce risk
Demonstrate how reinsurance or similar methods may be used to manage or reduce risk
Analyze how ALM and similar risk strategies can be used to manage or reduce risk in an organization
Demonstrate possible techniques for managing non-financial risks
Explain how to develop a capital model for a hypothetical organization

Demonstrate a conceptual understanding of economic measures of value and capital requirements (e.g., EVA, embedded value, economic capital, regulatory measures, and accounting measures) and their uses in decision-making processes
Apply risk measures (such as VaR and TVaR) and demonstrate how to use them in value and capital assessment
Demonstrate the use of techniques to allocate risk once aggregated
Propose techniques of attributing the “cost” of risk/capital strategies to business units in order to gauge performance (e.g. returns on marginal capital)
